name: transmitter_show
description: Hand the person the RC transmitter: a two-stick radio that drives the truck and flies the drone. By default it is docked: it waits on a fixed spot (on the table in front of them, or floating at lap height about 40 cm ahead) and does not move with their hands; they rest a thumb or index finger on each stick, the stick moves from where the finger touched, and lifting the finger centres it. Pinching its body and moving drags the dock; closing a hand round it and lifting holds it (handheld), and letting go sends it back to its dock. docked false makes it handheld: it appears between their hands and they pick it up. Truck: left stick throttle, right stick steering, buttons Horn and Reset. Drone (mode 2): left stick climbs and turns, right stick flies forward, back and sideways; buttons Take off/Land and Home/Reset; the switch picks easy steering (away from you is forward) or pro (the nose is forward). It already appears by itself when a truck or drone course opens. Use it when the person asks for the controller, the remote, the transmitter or the sticks, or asks how to drive or fly. Nothing is sent anywhere, so no confirmation is needed.

docked.description: Optional. true docks it on a fixed spot (the default), false makes it handheld.

name: transmitter_hide
description: Put the RC transmitter away: it lets go of both sticks (the truck coasts to a stop, the drone hovers) and disappears until transmitter_show or a new course brings it back. Use it when the person says put the controller away, hide the remote, or they are done driving.

name: transmitter_aids
description: Driving aids for the truck's training laps, all optional: training_speed (m/s, 0.3 to 1.2, default 0.6) is how fast a full left stick drives, slower is easier and the Autopilot learns that speed; steering_percent (50 to 100) is how much steering a full right stick gives; soft_centre makes small thumb moves small turns; steady_throttle makes one push of the left stick hold training speed so the person only steers (pull back to stop). Call it with no arguments to read them. Use it when the person says driving is too hard, too fast, too twitchy, or asks for cruise control. Nothing is sent anywhere.

training_speed.description: m/s at full left stick, 0.3 to 1.2.
